merger_name: CrowdStrike – intellectual property and associated technology assets of XM Cyber

anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, **CrowdStrike**) is a U.S. publicly listed holding company, incorporated under the laws of Delaware and headquartered in Texas, USA. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

CrowdStrike is active in cybersecurity services through its cloud-native Falcon platform, which provides protection for endpoints, cloud workloads, identities and data. CrowdStrike operates a software-as-a-service model, delivering its solutions via a unified cloud platform, and maintains a global presence with offices and operations across North America, Europe and Asia. CrowdStrike operates in Australia through its indirect wholly owned Australian subsidiary, CrowdStrike Australia Pty Ltd, with offices in Sydney.

CrowdStrike offers a broad range of cybersecurity products and services, including endpoint detection and response, identity protection, cloud security, threat intelligence and managed security services. Its Falcon platform is used by a diverse customer base across industries such as finance, healthcare, retail and government, enabling real-time threat monitoring, prevention and incident response across distributed IT environments.

XM Cyber Ltd (**XM Cyber**), including its subsidiaries, is an Israeli cybersecurity company. XM Cyber is currently an entity of the Schwarz Group.

XM Cyber specialises in continuous exposure management and attack path analysis solutions.

Schwarz Digits KG (**Schwarz Digits**), including its direct or indirect subsidiaries, is the digital and IT division of the Schwarz Group. Schwarz Digits’ core services include cloud, cyber security, data and AI, communication and Workspace for enterprise and public sector customers. Its offering mainly includes, among other things, a sovereign cloud solution through the STACKIT platform as well as other digital and AI-based services. Schwarz Digits is a global enterprise and will retain the infrastructure, personnel and capabilities to continue offering its digital services following the Acquisition.

Pursuant to an Asset Purchase Agreement, CrowdStrike is acquiring XM Cyber's intellectual property (including patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, domain names and source code) and associated technology (together, the **Transferred Assets**) (the **Acquisition**). CrowdStrike is not acquiring the shares of any XM Cyber entity, nor is it acquiring XM Cyber's existing employees.

Although XM Cyber’s intellectual property is primarily developed by its in-house product team based in Tel Aviv, the Transferred Assets include certain registered intellectual property rights in Australia – three registered trademarks, as well as one abandoned patent application, one abandoned trademark and two abandoned trademark applications (together, the **Australian Registered IP**). The Acquisition does not involve the transfer of any Australian business other than the Australian Registered IP.

determination_table_content.details:
CrowdStrike, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of CrowdStrike
Holdings, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, CrowdStrike), applied
for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of the
intellectual property (including patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade
secrets, domain names and source code) and associated
technology assets of XM Cyber Ltd. (XM Cyber), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, CrowdStrike, is a U.S. publicly listed holding company,
incorporated under the laws of Delaware and headquartered in
Texas, USA. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.’s shares are listed on the
Nasdaq stock exchange.
CrowdStrike is active in cybersecurity services through its cloud-
native Falcon platform, which provides protection for endpoints,
cloud workloads, identities and data. CrowdStrike operates a
software-as-a-service model, delivering its solutions via a unified
cloud platform, and maintains a global presence with offices and
operations across North America, Europe and Asia. CrowdStrike
operates in Australia through its indirect wholly owned Australian
subsidiary, CrowdStrike Australia Pty Ltd, with offices in Sydney.
CrowdStrike offers a broad range of cybersecurity products and
services, including endpoint detection and response, identity
protection, cloud security, threat intelligence and managed security
services. Its Falcon platform is used by a diverse customer base
across industries such as finance, healthcare, retail and government,
enabling real-time threat monitoring, prevention and incident
response across distributed IT environments.
The target, XM Cyber, including its subsidiaries, is an Israeli
cybersecurity company. XM Cyber is currently an entity of the
Schwarz Group. XM Cyber, specialises in continuous exposure
management and attack path analysis solutions.
In Australia, both CrowdStrike and XM Cyber supply enterprise
security software.
Schwarz Digits KG (Schwarz Digits), including its direct or indirect
subsidiaries, is the digital and IT division of the Schwarz Group.
Schwarz Digits’ core services include cloud, cyber security, data and
AI, communication and Workspace for enterprise and public sector
customers. Its offering mainly includes, among other things, a
sovereign cloud solution through the STACKIT platform as well as
other digital and AI-based services. Schwarz Digits is a global
enterprise and will retain the infrastructure, personnel and
capabilities to continue offering its digital services following the
Acquisition.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition, given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of enterprise
security software (as well as specific segments within
enterprise security software services) to customers in
Australia is low and the increase in share of supply arising
from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative global suppliers of enterprise security
software to customers in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
